newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Greenpeace blocks entry of maize ship to Portugal.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace blocks entry of maize ship to Portugal.

text.p: Some 30 protesters from the environmental group Greenpeace blocked the entry of a U.S. ship carrying genetically modified maize to a Lisbon harbour on Wednesday, witnesses said.
Five protesters chained themselves to the harbour wall and colleagues in four motorised dinghies harassed the "Pacificator" until the evening low tide prevented it from docking, they said.
"We will try again to stop the ship from entering when the tide rises," campaign coordinator Ricardo Aguilar told Reuters.
"We are protesting against gene-modified maize because it could be dangerous to the health of humans and animals," he added.

He echoed concern among Western environmentalists that genetic alterations could lead to an increase in the resistance of bacteria to antibiotics and could encourage insects to become more resistant to pesticide strains.
Protesters had painted the slogan "No X Corn" on the side of the ship, witnesses said. "X" means genetically-engineered, Aguilar said.
The maize, which was transported from Louisiana, was probably intended for use as cattle fodder, he said.
Portuguese police officers had witnessed the protest but made no arrests, he added.
